messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a spike in failed streaming sessions after the metadata-frame change landed in the runtime yesterday. Errors look like client parsers throwing on an unexpected '\u0001META' frame between data chunks.
kevin: Are these only older SDKs? which clients are failing?
tara: From initial logs: ios-sdk v1.3.0, python SDK <2.0, and a handful of homegrown proxy sidecars that parse raw frames. New JS & new Go SDKs are fine.
maria: Yep. We added an interstitial metadata frame for tooling info (trace id, model-version) per the streaming-rfc. New clients expect it; old ones barf.
devon: Rough count — ~0.7% of overall streaming traffic is failing with parse errors. 40% of those are from long-lived embedded devices (can't upgrade quick).
kevin: What's the quick mitigation? revert the change?
tara: Revert would be disruptive — we rely on metadata frames for trace propagation and adaptive routing. I'd prefer a temporary shim. Two options: 1) gateway strips metadata for flagged clients (proxy-level shim), 2) runtime emits metadata only when clients signal capability (negotiation header).
maria: Tradeoffs: gateway shim is fast to deploy and isolates client impact, but adds per-request proxy CPU and complicates edge code. Runtime negotiation keeps gateway simple but requires clients to send an opt-in header or handshake and needs rollout of negotiation support in some infra paths (gRPC, websocket, http-stream).
devon: Also: caching & batching. If gateway strips frames we still need to maintain KV cache keys identical across shapes. Stripping on the way out might change bytes and invalidate simple caches if we key on raw bytes.
kevin: Can we do detection heuristics? e.g., sniff first few frames and if unsupported frame found, fallback to legacy-mode for that connection. Add telemetry tag so we can count.
tara: Heuristic idea is okay — implement at gateway to avoid touching runtime kernel. Pseudocode:
```
if first_frame == DATA and next_frame == META and client not in known-capable-list:
  transform: remove META frames until handshake complete
  emit telemetry: shim_injected=true, client_hash=sha1(user-agent||ip)
else
  pass through
```
But beware: streaming is low-latency, extra copy could add ~0.5-2ms per packet. Need perf numbers.
maria: If we do gateway shim we must add a feature flag and an opt-out header for clients that need raw frames (internal infra).
devon: If we instead require client opt-in header (e.g., `x-rw-stream-v=2`), runtime can keep metadata and reject older clients with clear error. That accelerates migration but leaves stranded clients broken.
kevin: I'd vote for dual approach: quick gateway shim + migration telemetry, then flip to negotiate-only once adoption >95% or after a cutoff date.
tara: Agreed. Plan outline: 1) gateway shim rollout behind flag (targeted all ingress pods in us-east) 2) add telemetry counters: shim_injected, client_ua, error_code=PARSE_META 3) start client outreach (sdks, major customers) 4) after 4 weeks or 95% success, remove shim and enforce `x-rw-stream-v` negotiation.
maria: Ops checklist: - spike test in staging with synthetic legacy clients - measure p95 latency delta - add canary to 10% of traffic then 50% then 100% - create rollback trigger (error rate >1% or latency p95 +5ms)
devon: Also need to update docs + sdk changelogs. For sidecars we might provide a small backwards-compatible helper patch (python wrapper) so customers can opt-in to update without infra change.
kevin: Observability: dash for shim_injected, parse_errors, latency impact per-region, and sample traces where shim fired. Also surface a list of top client_ua buckets failing so support can contact them.
tara: Security: if gateway rewrites frames we must ensure no auth metadata is accidentally removed or mistaken for `META` frame. Let's whitelist fields that are safe to strip.
maria: I'll draft the rollout RFC addendum and include the decision to use gateway shim as short-term mitigation + negotiation header long-term. Can someone own the telemetry + dash?
devon: I can own telemetry + canary pipeline. I'll add the metrics to the runtime/gateway integration repo and create grafana panels.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging/gateway-shim v1 deployed to staging at 2024-08-01T14:02:11Z :rocket:
kevin: Great. After staging smoke I'll open a customers/outreach doc for the SDK teams.
maria: Thanks — will post RFC addendum in #eng-platform and ping SDK leads.
tara: One more note: update the client capability registry (internal) so we can map versions to supported stream format.
maria: Cool. We'll revisit in 48h after staging metrics. :thumbsup:
